title: The Health Care Affordability Elections of 2026 and 2028
discussion_signal: The post frames health costs as a household and political-choice constraint crossing party lines. It links affordability pressure to delayed care, insurance and out-of-pocket decisions, retail-health experimentation, and the possibility that patients become more active consumers because formal coverage does not remove practical cost exposure.
linked_research_question: How do health-cost discussions connect household adaptation, care choices, political legitimacy, and new routes to access?
limits: The post summarizes a poll and does not establish causal political effects
LinkedIn engagement is not a representative patient sample
